newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tankers mainly steady, West Africa dips.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tankers mainly steady, West Africa dips.

text.p: Dirty tanker rates were mainly steady on Wednesday but West Africa rates continued to dip, especially 130,000 tonne vessels, brokers said.

"There have been a lot of VLCCs (very large crude carriers) done in the last one and a half or two weeks. The more interest there is in VLCCs, the less there is in Suezmaxes (130,000 tonners)," one broker said.
West Africa/U.S. Suezmaxes edged down to W97.5-100 from W100 on Tuesday, while VLCCs were steady at about W72.5 in quiet trade.

Middle East rates were also unchanged at W57.5 for a VLCC to Europe, while the ultra-large crude carrier Mare Champion was said done at W52.5 for 315,000 tonnes for Total, loading 315,000 tonnes on April 15 to UKC. The even bigger Stena King was fixed at W59 for 450,000 tonnes to the U.S. Gulf for Vela, loading April 25.
VLCCs to Japan were unchanged at W67.5 and to Singapore at W62.5
The 130,000 tonne cross-Mediterranean market was steady at W135/140, with Norwegian destinations at the higher end due to tight tonnage, brokers said.
The North Sea/transatlantic sector was unchanged at W75/77.5 for VLCCs, while cross-Med rates were also flat at W105 for 130,000 tonners and W110 for 80,000 vessels.
"Yesterday and the day before were a bit busier but there is still good activity," an Italian Med broker said.
Inter-U.K./Cont 25,000 tonne fuel oil edged up to W200 from W195 on fair enquiry, while cross-Med rates were steady at W210.
In the Caribs/upcoast market, 70,000 tonne crude cargoes continued to firm to W210, with 50,000 tonne fuel oil at W210/215 on a lack of tonnage, brokers said.
